# nagios_nna_nmap_scan (Resource)

Manages a Nagios Network Analyzer scheduled Nmap scan - a set of nmap flags run on a recurring schedule. Its `id` is what an `nmap`-type `nagios_nna_check` references as `object_id`.

Each `schedule_type` takes a fixed set of `schedule_parameters` keys, which are checked at plan time because Network Analyzer itself accepts anything:

| `schedule_type` | required `schedule_parameters` |
|---|---|
| `every` | `x` - run every `x` minutes |
| `hourlyAt` | `minute` (0-59) |
| `dailyAt` | `time` (`HH:MM`) |
| `weeklyOn` | `weekday` (0-6), `time` |
| `monthlyOn` | `day` (1-31), `time` |
| `yearlyOn` | `month` (1-12), `day`, `time` |
| `cron` | `cron` - a five-field cron expression |

Network Analyzer's own UI can also restrict a schedule with `days` and `between` list parameters; those are not supported here, and a scan that has them fails to refresh rather than having them silently erased on the next apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A reusable profile (optional - a scan's own `parameters` is what runs).
resource "nagios_nna_nmap_profile" "quick" {
  name       = "quick-tcp-sweep"
  parameters = "-sS -T4 -F -e eth0"
}

# Sweep the DMZ every night at 02:00.
resource "nagios_nna_nmap_scan" "dmz_nightly" {
  name            = "dmz-nightly"
  nmap_profile_id = nagios_nna_nmap_profile.quick.id

  # Network Analyzer requires a standalone "-e <interface>" flag, and the
  # target goes in the same string.
  parameters = "-sS -T4 -F -e eth0 10.20.0.0/24"

  schedule_type       = "dailyAt"
  schedule_parameters = { time = "02:00" }
}

# Other recurrences take different parameters:
#
#   schedule_type = "every"      schedule_parameters = { x = "15" }
#   schedule_type = "hourlyAt"   schedule_parameters = { minute = "30" }
#   schedule_type = "weeklyOn"   schedule_parameters = { weekday = "1", time = "03:00" }
#   schedule_type = "monthlyOn"  schedule_parameters = { day = "1", time = "03:00" }
#   schedule_type = "yearlyOn"   schedule_parameters = { month = "3", day = "14", time = "04:00" }
#   schedule_type = "cron"       schedule_parameters = { cron = "*/5 * * * *" }
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of this scan. Network Analyzer does not require it to be unique.
- `parameters` (String) The nmap command-line flags and scan target, as a single free-form string (for example `-sS -T4 -F -e eth0 10.0.0.0/24`). Network Analyzer requires a standalone `-e <interface>` flag: the space-separated short form only, with an interface name that is not a `<placeholder>`. Network Analyzer checks this on create but not on update, so the provider checks it at plan time for both. The interface name itself is not checked for existence. Note this string is a command line Network Analyzer executes server-side on every scheduled run, so treat it as privileged input: anyone able to change it in configuration can influence what the Network Analyzer host runs (scan targets, `--script` NSE selection, output paths). The provider deliberately does not try to sanitize it, since restricting nmap's own flag syntax would defeat the purpose of the attribute.
- `schedule_parameters` (Map of String) The recurrence detail for `schedule_type`, as string values - see the resource description for the keys each type takes. Values are always strings, e.g. `{ weekday = "1", time = "03:00" }`.
- `schedule_type` (String) How the scan recurs: one of `cron`, `dailyAt`, `every`, `hourlyAt`, `monthlyOn`, `weeklyOn`, or `yearlyOn`. Determines which `schedule_parameters` keys are required.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the scan runs on its schedule. Defaults to true (Network Analyzer's own default when the field is omitted is false, which would silently create an idle scan).
- `ndiffs_enabled` (Boolean) Whether Network Analyzer compares each run against the previous one with ndiff.
- `nmap_profile_id` (Number) The ID of a `nagios_nna_nmap_profile` this scan is based on. Optional: `parameters` is what actually runs. If the profile is later deleted, Network Analyzer clears this reference, which Terraform will then plan to restore (and fail to, since the profile is gone) until the configuration is updated.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The numeric ID Network Analyzer assigns this scan. Like other Network Analyzer resources it's addressed by ID rather than name.
- `last_run_at` (String) When the scan last ran. Empty until it first runs. Managed entirely server-side and read-only.
- `times_ran` (Number) How many times the scan has run. Managed entirely server-side and read-only.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Scheduled scans are imported by the numeric ID Network Analyzer assigns
# them, not by name - the same ID an nmap-type nagios_nna_check references
# as object_id.
terraform import nagios_nna_nmap_scan.example 7

# Caveat: a scan whose schedule was restricted with Network Analyzer's own
# "days" or "between" options can't be imported or refreshed - those are
# stored as lists, which this resource cannot represent, and it errors
# rather than silently erasing them on the next apply.
```
